era_footprint.wpa2_era: widespread on enterprise WLCs; canonical LEAP deployments
era_footprint.wpa3_era: Catalyst 9800 + Meraki cloud APs support WPA3-Personal / Enterprise
era_footprint.wifi6_6e_era: Catalyst 9130 / Meraki MR57 / MR56 lines; Wi-Fi 6E support 2022+

technical_body.attack_surface_summary: Historical LEAP (asleap crack), enterprise MSCHAPv2 capture via rogue RADIUS, WLC WIDS to evade.

era_footprint.wpa2_era: AC-Pro / AC-LR / AC-Lite were the workhorses ~2015–2020
era_footprint.wpa3_era: UniFi 6 / U6-LR / U6-Pro / U6-Enterprise support WPA3-Personal and transition mode
era_footprint.wifi6_6e_era: U6-Enterprise / U6-Mesh support Wi-Fi 6E on 6 GHz UNII-5/6/7/8

notable_defaults: 802.11r/k/v enabled by default on modern controllers
technical_body.attack_surface_summary: Transition-mode downgrade against UniFi 6 with legacy clients; FT-handshake capture on 11r roams; UniFi controller ships default WPA2 evil-twin targets.

era_footprint.wpa2_era: Archer C7 / C1200 / C2300 were the volume plays; WPS PIN derivation viable on many generations
era_footprint.wpa3_era: Archer AX line (AX10/AX50/AX55/AX73) supports WPA3-Personal from 2019+
era_footprint.wifi6_6e_era: Archer AXE / Deco XE lines support Wi-Fi 6E

technical_body.attack_surface_summary: WPS with vendor-derivable PIN algorithms on older generations; Realtek chipset on cheaper models (RTL8xxx CVE surface); AP firmware update discipline is variable.

era_footprint.wpa2_era: Widespread on WISP and small-ISP deployments 2010+
era_footprint.wifi6_6e_era: hAP ax² / hAP ax³ / cAP ax lines support Wi-Fi 6

notable_defaults: hostapd underneath but exposed through RouterOS wireless config
default admin creds on old RouterBOARDs are a persistent problem
technical_body.attack_surface_summary: Unusual RouterOS beacon fingerprints (see AP fingerprinting); administrative interface CVEs are OUT OF SCOPE (see plan-knowledge.md scope rule).

era_footprint.wpa2_era: R710 / R610 workhorses in enterprise deployments 2015+

technical_body.attack_surface_summary: Aggressive WIDS on SmartZone — noisy attacks get logged; enterprise cert-pinning discipline typically strong; targets are the misconfigured 802.1X profiles, not the AP itself.

name: Consumer mesh (eero / Google Nest WiFi / TP-Link Deco / Netgear Orbi)

era_footprint.wpa2_era: eero Gen 1 / 2, Google WiFi Gen 1, Orbi RBK50 — WPA2-Personal only
era_footprint.wpa3_era: eero 6 / 6+ / Pro 6, Nest WiFi Pro, Deco X60 / X68, Orbi RBK850 all support WPA3-Personal (mostly in transition mode by default)
era_footprint.wifi6_6e_era: eero Pro 6E, Nest WiFi Pro (6E), Deco XE75, Orbi RBKE960 support Wi-Fi 6E

notable_defaults: WPA3 transition mode almost universally the default in 2024–2026
802.11k/v enabled by default; 11r off on many for compatibility
technical_body.attack_surface_summary: The dominant WPA3-transition-downgrade target class. Aggressive band-steering makes MC-MitM effective. Kr00k tail exists on Broadcom-based older units. Captive-portal cred capture works well against guest-network configurations.
